chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah together, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Indeed, Adam (peace be upon him) fell ill and craved fruit, so Habbatullah went to seek fruit for him. Gabriel met him and said to him: 'Where are you going, O Habbatullah?' He said: 'Adam is ill and he craves fruit.' Gabriel said to him: 'Return, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has taken his soul.' He returned and found that Allah had taken his soul. The angels washed him, then they placed him, and commanded Habbatullah to step forward and pray over him. He stepped forward and prayed over him while the angels were behind him. Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, revealed to him to say five Takbirs over him and to say Taslim, and to level his grave. Then He said: 'Thus, do with your dead.'

key_terms.غَسَّلَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ: The angels washed him (ritual washing of the body)
key_terms.يُكَبِّرَ عَلَيْهِ خَمْسًا: To say five Takbirs over him

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual steps and number of Takbirs for the funeral prayer according to this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes the precedent for the five Takbirs in the funeral prayer by narrating the death of Prophet Adam (peace be upon him), where his son Seth (Habbatullah) led the angels in prayer. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that Adam’s funeral rites serve as the archetype for human burial practices, specifically emphasizing the Imam's precedence in leading the prayer and the specific ritual of squaring the grave. The narration underscores the continuity of divine instruction from the first human to the community of believers regarding funeral jurisprudence.
